numericPolicy.label: ENGINE_POLICY, not an official Spine accuracy standard
numericPolicy.formula: hypot((wx-start.x)/L-(dx/L)*(joint/N), (wy-start.y)/L-(dy/L)*(joint/N)), L=hypot(dx,dy), joints 0..N including final tip
numericPolicy.reason: Chain-scale accuracy avoids accepting 100% displacement loss just because the absolute world origin is huge. Normalize before multiplying to avoid underflowing tiny absolute tolerances or ideal tiny displacements. Reject nonfinite world positions/error. No geometry correction, origin rebasing, world-origin-relative tolerance or arbitrary ban on large coordinates.
numericPolicy.toleranceRationale: 1e-10 provides margin above the normal 256*EPSILON magnitude (~5.7e-14), while enforcing geometry much finer than chain length. This is an engineering choice, not a universal floating-point error theorem.
